scenarios.name: empty-result
scenarios.schedule: one RR transaction: contradictory balance bounds, text C boundary and full table queries; commit

scenarios.name: insert-phantom
scenarios.schedule: two RR transactions each completely read active=true as empty; each inserts a different active=true row; both commit

scenarios.name: delete-reinsert
scenarios.schedule: one RR transaction reads, deletes with actual new tombstone, reads empty, reinserts with tombstone predecessor, reads; commit

scenarios.name: cross-predicate-update
scenarios.schedule: RR A reads complete east set, B reads complete west set; A moves id1 east->west, B moves id2 west->east; both commit

scenarios.name: rr-write-skew
scenarios.schedule: RR A/B completely read active=true as two rows; each deactivates its own row; both commit

scenarios.name: serializable-abort-retry
scenarios.schedule: SSI A/B completely read active=true as two rows; each attempts own deactivation; exactly one server 40001/40P01 abort; retry with fresh TX id reads remaining active set and preserves last active row

scenarios.name: same-value-new-version
scenarios.schedule: RR transaction performs two same-content UPDATEs with distinct server tokens and reads each intermediate version; commit; a second transaction reads final version

scenarios.name: savepoint-complete-query
scenarios.schedule: RR transaction uses repeated same-name savepoint identities, updates then deletes, reads empty, restores child then parent, full queries retain delivered observations; commit
